title: Cost Literacy Labflow: Interactive onboarding labs for Console empty projects
creator: Arielle Nguyen
description:
Problem: New users land in an empty Console project and often create demo traffic that leads to confusion about cost and token usage. Current empty states and static tutorials teach features but do not build cost literacy or safe-to-try workflows. Goal: Design an interactive "Cost Literacy Labflow" — a guided, hands-on onboarding experience embedded in the empty project canvas that teaches safe APIs, simulated traffic, cost previewing, and quick templates for low-cost experiments.

Scope: design UX patterns, microcopy, 3 interactive lab templates (Chat demo, Embeddings search, Batch inferencing), an inline cost-preview simulator, tooltip-driven explainers, and fallback empty-state variations for users on Dedicated/Private plans. Deliverables: Figma prototype (high-fidelity), clickable flows for A/B variants (guided vs. exploratory), copy package for tooltips and banners, acceptance criteria, and a design spec for engineers including accessibility notes and animation guidance.

Success metrics: increase time-to-first-successful-inference (TTFSI) within the free credit window; reduce first-week accidental high-cost incidents by 40%; increase activation (first API call with valid model selection) from 28% to 45% for new projects.

Acceptance criteria:
- Three lab templates complete with step definitions, success states, and rollback guidance.
- Inline cost simulator that shows estimated token cost and latency for a single run and 1k-run projection (UI only, mocked data).
- Tooltip glossary for tokens, KV cache, batching that opens inline details and linkouts to docs.
- Variant A (Linear guide) and Variant B (Quick-play) prototypes for A/B usability testing.
- Developer handoff spec with component list, micro-interactions, and copy.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Runtime cost simulator will be mocked in MVP; accuracy vs. speed trade-off documented for engineering.
- Too many tooltips can overwhelm; propose progressive disclosure tied to user signals (e.g., when they select a large sequence length or batch size).
- Dedicated/Private customers need customizable messaging; include conditional copy slots and an admin toggle.

Implementation notes for engineers (links below):
- Prototype calls out a lightweight telemetry event schema for tracking clicks, completions, and cost-acknowledgements.
- UX should avoid blocking core workflows; labs sit in an "Experiment" tab in the empty project and are dismissible via a persistent "Try later" button.

Rollout plan:
1) Internal prototype review with PM/Eng/Research (Mar 12)
2) Moderated usability sessions with 8 new signups (Mar 15–19)
3) Iterate and freeze design (Mar 22)
4) Engineering spike + API mocks (Mar 25–Apr 5)
5) Beta enablement for new free-tier projects (Apr 15)
